prerequisites: Ability to write simple procedural programs in any programming language.
Ability to trace and debug small programs.
Knowledge of basic data structures, such as arrays and lists.
Knowledge of the principles of object-oriented programming, including abstract classes and inheritance.

learning_outcomes.text: Describe fundamental algorithmic paradigms and data structures.
Analyze the computational complexity of algorithms.
Compare algorithmic solutions based on their performance and constraints.
Implement algorithms in the C programming language.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to programming in the C language.
Algorithm specification: computational model, computational problem, algorithm.
Algorithm analysis: elements of combinatorics and asymptotic analysis, mathematical induction, complexity analysis, and correctness analysis.
Trees: definitions, properties, and traversals. Binary trees.
Search trees: definitions and special cases. Binary search trees; (2,4)-trees.
Graphs: definitions, properties, data structures for graph representation, graph traversals (BFS and DFS), shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, and topological sorting.
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes, wooclap)

assessment_methods.method: Written examination: Algorithm analysis and design in pseudocode
Written examination: Implementation of algorithms in C

assessment_rules: A mandatory written examination consists of three parts: theory questions, algorithm analysis and design in pseudocode, and implementation of algorithms in C. An oral follow-up assessment may be required to verify that the submitted written examination accurately reflects the student’s individual knowledge and competencies. Generative AI Tools are permitted for individual study and self-assessment but not during the final examination.
